faq.question: What is Canli Capital?
faq.answer: Canli Capital is an open-source lab that connects AI agents to financial data and quant tools they can check. It publishes MCP servers, company financials traced to SEC filings, open benchmarks and its own paper-trading record, failures included.

faq.question: What is canli-mcp?
faq.answer: canli-mcp is one MCP server that loads every Canli Capital server in one process. The model sees three tools, find_tool, describe_tool and run_tool, and behind them sit 285 tools for quant finance, backtest validation, SEC filings, fundamentals, rates, prices and paper trading.

faq.question: How do I add canli-mcp to Claude, Cursor or another AI assistant?
faq.answer: In Claude Code, run claude mcp add canli -- npx -y canli-mcp. In Cursor, Claude Desktop or any other MCP client, add a server named canli whose command is npx with the arguments -y and canli-mcp. It needs Node.js 20.10 or later and no account.

faq.question: How does canli-mcp compare with OpenBB, EdgarTools and Yahoo Finance MCP?
faq.answer: With the same model and questions, canli-mcp answered 79% of the questions every server finished correctly, against 54% for the best of the others, and it sends the model 859 tokens of tools on every request. We wrote the questions, so read the caveats too.

link.text: See every run and the caveats.

faq.question: Where does the data come from?
faq.answer: From the original publishers: companies' filings with the SEC, the US Treasury's daily yield curves, FRED for economic series and Yahoo Finance chart data for prices. Answers drawn from data name their source, and answers from a filing carry its accession number.

faq.question: How do I check whether my backtest is overfit?
faq.answer: Send the returns your backtest produced to the validators. The deflated Sharpe ratio corrects for how many variants you tried, the probability of backtest overfitting compares those variants with each other, and the minimum track record length says how much history the Sharpe ratio needs.

faq.question: Is it free?
faq.answer: Yes. The MCP servers and the code are free and MIT-licensed, the published data is CC BY 4.0, and the hosted API has fair-use limits. No paid plan is offered.

faq.question: Does my data leave my computer?
faq.answer: The quant and validation tools run on your machine and send nothing anywhere. The data tools fetch public data from the SEC, the Treasury, FRED, Yahoo Finance or canlicapital.com, and send only the company, series or symbol you asked for.

link.text: See the setup and local mode.

faq.question: Are your strategies trading real capital?
faq.answer: No. ALPHAC, Canli Capital's trading engine, runs its strategies on paper, and the record says so on every page. Paper results do not establish what real trading would return.

link.text: Inspect the record and its basis.

faq.question: Can I invest or copy the trades?
faq.answer: Canli Capital is a research project, not a fund or investment adviser. This site does not offer managed capital or copy-trading.
